newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor talks to sell Nesher Cement stake.
newsitem.headline: Koor talks to sell Nesher Cement stake.

text.p: Israel's Koor Industries Ltd is negotiating with four foreign companies for the sale of a 20 percent stake of Nesher Cement, a Koor source who spoke on condition of anonymity said on Thursday.
A company spokeswoman refused to comment.
Talks were underway with France's Lafarge, Mexico's Cemex, Italy's Italcementi and Switzerland's Holderbank, the source said.

Nesher Cement -- which is controlled by Mashav Initiating and Development Ltd, a joint venture of Koor and Clal Israel -- has been seeking a partner for more than a year as a means of breaking into the Middle East market. In Israel, the company has a monopoly on cement production.
Nesher's sales suffered in 1996 after Israel closed off the Palestinian West Bank and Gaza Strip out of security concerns. There was also as a decline in residential building starts in Israel.

In addition, Israel and Jordan signed a trade pact in 1996. Under it, Jordan exported 150,000 tonnes of cement to the Palestinian territories in 1996, cutting into Nesher's market there. Jordan also exported limited quantities of cement to Israel last year.
